title: INDOPACOM: large disc using clouds as concealment

tellings.quote: Large disc using clouds as concealment.

plain: A large saucer came out of a thick bank of cloud over the Pacific and slipped back into it, as if hiding once it knew it was watched, according to a case Michels reads out on his show with Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official who says he wrote the Immaculate Constellation report, an unsigned paper entered into the record of a congressional hearing on 13 November 2024 that the Defense Department says matches no program it knows of. The report describes infrared satellite footage of "a large saucer shaped UAP emerging from within a dense cloud formation", UAP being the government's term for unidentified objects, and says its dip back "implied that the saucer shaped UAP had become aware that it was under observation". That it was hiding is the report's own inference, from footage it describes in words and does not show.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report's case "INDOPACOM Large Disc Using Clouds as Concealment" describes "OPIR footage of a large saucer shaped UAP emerging from within a dense cloud formation" and reads its dip back into the clouds as behavior that "implied that the saucer shaped UAP had become aware that it was under observation". Jesse Michels reads out the heading, so the concealment is the report's inference from footage it describes in words and does not show.
